criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies handbook minimum wage ($14.00) is below CO 2025 minimum ($14.81)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 states the $14.00 handbook floor is below the $14.81 2025 Colorado minimum and is non-compliant.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies $0.81/hour gap or back-pay liability risk
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 states the floor is $0.81 below the state minimum and recommends back wages.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Notes that 389 hourly non-exempt employees are potentially affected
criteria_results.reasoning: C-1 lists the affected population as all 389 hourly employees.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing daily overtime rule (12-hour daily threshold)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-3 finds that section 4.3 covers only the 40-hour weekly trigger and omits COMPS Order #39's 12-hour daily trigger.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Notes relevance to healthcare 12-hour shift schedules
criteria_results.reasoning: C-3 ties daily overtime to a 24/7 care operator running 12-hour CNA/LPN/RN shifts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies incorrect meal break threshold (6 hours vs. required 5 hours)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-4 flags the six-hour meal trigger against Colorado's five-hour rule.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies rest breaks are mandatory, not merely 'encouraged'
criteria_results.reasoning: C-5 flags 'encouraged but not required' as affirmatively non-compliant with COMPS Rule 5.2.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Specifies rest breaks must be paid 10-minute breaks per 4 hours
criteria_results.reasoning: C-5 states COMPS Order #39 Rule 5.2 requires a paid 10-minute rest period per four hours or major fraction.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies PTO accrual rate (1:40) is below HFWA minimum (1:30)
criteria_results.reasoning: C-6 identifies 1:40 accrual against the HFWA 1:30 minimum.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Notes combined PTO bank must meet sick leave accrual floor
criteria_results.reasoning: C-6 explains that a combined PTO bank satisfies HFWA only if it meets HFWA accrual, use and protection rules.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies complete omission of Public Health Emergency Leave (PHEL)
criteria_results.reasoning: H-2 identifies that PHEL is completely omitted and describes the 80-hour entitlement.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies complete omission of Colorado FAMLI program
criteria_results.reasoning: H-1 and the executive summary state the handbook never mentions FAMLI and covers only FMLA; benefits payable since Jan 1, 2024.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Notes FAMLI provides up to 12 weeks (16 for pregnancy complications)
criteria_results.reasoning: States 12 weeks of FAMLI leave (16 with pregnancy/childbirth complications).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Notes FAMLI premium sharing or eligibility differs from FMLA
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes the $2,500 base-period eligibility vs FMLA's 12 months/1,250 hours and the 0.9% premium split 0.45%/0.45%.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies PTO forfeiture-on-resignation as illegal under CO law
criteria_results.reasoning: C-10 finds forfeiture unlawful, citing C.R.S. 8-4-101(14)(a)(III) and Nieto: no forfeiture regardless of the reason for separation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Notes CO prohibits use-it-or-lose-it / forfeiture policies for PTO
criteria_results.reasoning: States forfeiture is barred regardless of the reason for separation and recommends payout on any separation, voluntary or involuntary, with the legal basis given.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies blanket 'next regular payday' final pay policy as non-compliant
criteria_results.reasoning: C-8 identifies the blanket next-payday rule as unlawful for involuntary terminations and explains the timing differs by separation type.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Specifies CO final pay tiers (involuntary: immediate/6hrs; quit with notice: last day; quit without notice: next payday or 10 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: Describes the involuntary tier (immediate, or within 6 hours of the next workday) and next-regular-payday timing for quits, and recites the notice-based quit tiers (Section 6). That covers at least two tiers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies non-compete applied to all employees violates CO threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: C-9 identifies that a blanket non-compete on all employees is void under C.R.S. 8-2-113 below the highly compensated threshold.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: References $123,750 compensation threshold for non-compete enforceability
criteria_results.reasoning: References the $123,750 threshold (calling it the 2024 figure) and applies the updated $127,091 figure; the threshold number is present and discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes most employees fall below the $123,750 non-compete threshold
criteria_results.reasoning: Quantifies that at most 23 of 612 employees can be bound and at least 589 cannot.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing notice and right-to-consult-attorney disclosure
criteria_results.reasoning: Flags the missing separate, clear-and-conspicuous signed notice, but never mentions the worker's right to consult an attorney, which the criterion explicitly requires.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies non-solicitation without compensation threshold ($74,250)
criteria_results.reasoning: Identifies that the customer non-solicit applies to all employees but needs 60% of the threshold; references $74,250 (as the 2024 figure) and $76,254.60.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Quantifies employees below non-solicitation threshold using census data
criteria_results.reasoning: Uses the census to show at most 90 employees are eligible and at least 522 cannot be bound.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies omission of sexual orientation from EEO protected classes
criteria_results.reasoning: H-5 lists sexual orientation as a missing CADA class under C.R.S. 24-34-402.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies omission of gender identity/gender expression from EEO list
criteria_results.reasoning: H-5 lists gender identity and gender expression as missing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies omission of marital status from EEO protected classes
criteria_results.reasoning: H-5 lists marital status as missing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies omission of ancestry and/or creed from EEO protected classes
criteria_results.reasoning: H-5 lists creed and ancestry as missing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies omission of genetic information from EEO protected classes
criteria_results.reasoning: H-5 lists genetic information as missing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_013: Identifies missing reference to Colorado Civil Rights Division (CCRD)
criteria_results.reasoning: M-4 identifies that section 3.3 names only the EEOC and omits the CCRD.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Identifies social media policy as overbroad / potentially violating NLRA Section 7
criteria_results.reasoning: H-9 finds the prior-approval social media rule overbroad under NLRA Section 7 (Stericycle) because it chills concerted discussion of working conditions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_014: Notes Colorado lawful off-duty activities protection
criteria_results.reasoning: H-9 and the executive summary cite C.R.S. 24-34-402.5 (lawful off-duty conduct) against the social media policy.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015: Identifies progressive discipline language may undermine at-will status
criteria_results.reasoning: M-6 and Q4 identify that the mandatory 'will be given the opportunity to improve' language can create an implied contract (Keenan) despite the at-will disclaimer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_015: Recommends qualifying progressive discipline with discretionary language
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends permissive 'may include' language, deleting the sentence, and cross-referencing section 1.3.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016: Identifies arbitration clause fails to carve out non-arbitrable claims
criteria_results.reasoning: H-10 notes the clause lacks carve-outs for workers' compensation, unemployment and FAMLI determinations.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_016: Identifies arbitration clause lacks agency charge-filing preservation
criteria_results.reasoning: H-10 notes the missing carve-out for administrative charges and cites Waffle House on agency charges.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017: Identifies missing whistleblower/retaliation protection policy
criteria_results.reasoning: H-7 identifies no standalone whistleblower policy and cites C.R.S. 8-2-123, 8-14.4-101 and 8-4-120.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_017: Notes particular importance for healthcare employer
criteria_results.reasoning: H-7 frames the gap as significant for a licensed health-care operator, covering patient-safety reporting.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_004: Does not flag mandatory arbitration as per se unenforceable
criteria_results.reasoning: Calls the clause likely unenforceable 'as drafted' for specific defects and suggests a standalone agreement; never says mandatory arbitration is per se unlawful.
